reports.name: Strategy

snapshot.holdings: 851,305 BTC as of Nov 22, 2026 (avg cost $75,446/BTC, total cost ~$64.23B)

reports.email_summary: Strategy keeps buying BTC but at a trickle while STRC buybacks dominate cash and mNAV sits near/below 1x.
reports.bottom_line: BTC-per-share accretion continues (13 straight weeks per Saylor) but at a shrinking pace as weekly BTC buys fell to just 457 coins while STRC preferred buybacks absorbed 7x more cash; with mNAV hovering near parity (0.97-1.07x depending on measure) and BTC sitting ~$9.6-12B underwater, the equity-issuance flywheel that powers the thesis is stalling, though management has avoided value-destructive raises so far.
source_conflicts: mNAV estimates for the week vary by source and methodology: TheBlock showed ~0.68-0.69x (Nov 19-20), mnav.com showed 1.01x (Nov 20), BloFin's dashboard-based calc showed 0.78x-1.07x depending on definition (Nov 17), and cryptoticker reported 0.97x (Nov 20) — basic market-cap-only vs. enterprise-value vs. company-dashboard methodologies diverge meaningfully at these compressed levels.
Unrealized BTC loss estimates range from ~$9.6B to ~$13.7B depending on the exact BTC price snapshot and date used across sources this week.

updates.headline: Strategy buys just 457 BTC, STRC buyback 7x larger
updates.what_happened: Strategy disclosed in an 8-K that between Nov 16-22 it sold 1,925,676 Class A shares for $176.7 million net proceeds, using only $29.6 million (17%) to buy 457 BTC at an average of $64,898/coin, while the remaining $211.8 million funded STRC preferred buybacks — roughly seven times the bitcoin spend. Total holdings rose to 851,305 BTC at an average cost of $75,446.
updates.thesis_fit: BTC accumulation pace continues to shrink and capital is being redirected toward preferred buybacks rather than new BTC, muting the stock's effective exposure to further BTC upside.

updates.headline: Board raises preferred-stock buyback cap to $4 billion
updates.what_happened: Strategy's board approved increasing the authorized aggregate purchase price under its digital credit securities (preferred stock) repurchase program from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion, with $1.12 billion remaining available as of Nov 22. The company also authorized reallocating up to $1.0 billion from the USD Reserve to USD Cash, which dropped the USD Reserve to $3.73 billion from $4.75 billion the prior week.
updates.thesis_fit: Expands flexibility to retire discounted preferred stock, which can be accretive to common equity, but further depletes the cash buffer that supports BTC buying and dividend coverage.

updates.headline: Saylor claims 13 straight weeks of BTC-per-share gains
updates.what_happened: Michael Saylor said on X that Strategy's net Bitcoin per share rose for a 13th consecutive week, equivalent to a 2,505 BTC gain worth $199 million before preferred dividends, or 584 satoshis per share cumulatively. The company paid $17.6 million in preferred dividends and spent $211.8 million on STRC buybacks during the same week.
updates.thesis_fit: Directly addresses the core thesis metric (BTC per diluted share), showing continued per-share accretion even as absolute BTC buying slows and dividends/buybacks consume most new capital.

updates.headline: mNAV falls near or below 1.0x as BTC crashes
updates.what_happened: Strategy's mNAV touched roughly 0.97x on the company's own metric Nov 20 and as low as 0.68-0.78x on simple market-cap methodologies as Bitcoin fell toward $55,673, a two-year low, before partially recovering. MSTR stock fell to around $81-86 intraday during the week, down over 20% in five trading days at one point.
updates.thesis_fit: A sub-1.0x or near-parity mNAV stalls the equity-issuance flywheel that historically let Strategy raise accretive capital to buy more BTC per share.

updates.headline: Peter Schiff renews 'complete fraud' attack on Saylor
updates.what_happened: As MSTR stock fell nearly 23% over the week to $86.13 by Nov 19, bitcoin critic Peter Schiff renewed public criticism of Strategy's business model, calling it a "complete fraud" in response to Saylor's investor Q&A, arguing the company lacks a viable underlying business.
updates.thesis_fit: High-profile public critique amplifies bearish sentiment during a period of falling mNAV and widening unrealized BTC losses, adding reputational/narrative pressure on the stock.

updates.headline: Strategy buys 485 BTC, spending drops 59% week-over-week
updates.what_happened: Strategy disclosed buying 485 BTC for $33.4 million (avg $68,887/coin) during the week ended Nov 15, down 59% in dollar terms from the prior week's $81.9 million purchase, while funding the bulk of a $244.7 million stock sale toward STRC buybacks rather than BTC. Holdings reached 850,849 BTC with no BTC sales reported.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued deceleration in BTC buying pace as the price fell, reinforcing the pattern of prioritizing preferred-stock buybacks over fresh Bitcoin accumulation.

reports.name: Metaplanet
reports.email_summary: Metaplanet redirects CB proceeds to buybacks, formally convenes Dec 18 EGM, shares hit multi-year low as mNAV sinks near 0.46x.
reports.bottom_line: No new dilution or incremental BTC buying was disclosed this week; instead, management confirmed it is steering October convertible-bond proceeds into share buybacks below mNAV rather than new equity-funded Bitcoin purchases, which is non-dilutive and BTC-per-share accretive. However, the stock continued falling to fresh lows with mNAV compressing toward ~0.46-0.6x ahead of the Nov 30 MSCI exclusion, underscoring persistent valuation and financing-capacity pressure.
source_conflicts: mNAV estimates vary by source and date (0.49x on Nov 12 per bitcointreasuries.net-based calc, 0.6-0.61x on Nov 16-17 post-earnings per Japanese trackers, 0.46x implied by PBR on Nov 20 per Kabutan) — likely reflects fast-moving price/BTC-price inputs rather than a true conflict, but figures should not be treated as interchangeable.

Some third-party trackers (bitcointreasuries.net cached pages) still show 43,000 BTC as of Jul/Oct 2026, while Metaplanet's own Q3 disclosure and most financial media confirm 44,000 BTC as of Sept 30, 2026.

updates.headline: Metaplanet to use CB proceeds for buybacks, not BTC
updates.what_happened: Reporting on Metaplanet's capital allocation plans indicates the company is prioritizing share repurchases over additional Bitcoin purchases with proceeds from its October convertible bond issue. Between October 14 and November 12 the company spent roughly ¥28.3 billion repurchasing shares, including about 12.3 million shares for ¥3.0 billion in the November 1-12 window alone.
updates.thesis_fit: Directing non-dilutive debt proceeds into buybacks executed below 1.0x mNAV is accretive to BTC per share and avoids further equity dilution, consistent with the thesis's preference for buybacks over dilutive issuance.

updates.headline: Metaplanet formally convenes Dec 18 EGM on capital reduction
updates.what_happened: Metaplanet filed timely disclosures ('Notice of Convocation for the Extraordinary General Meeting' and a virtual-attendance guide) confirming the previously announced capital stock/reserve reduction to ¥1 will be voted on at a virtual EGM on December 18, 2026, with an effective date around December 30, 2026.
updates.thesis_fit: This is procedural formalization of the already-disclosed capital reduction plan (to expand distributable reserves for buybacks/dividends) rather than a change in terms.

updates.headline: MSCI confirms Metaplanet removal effective Nov 30
updates.what_happened: MSCI's official filings confirmed Metaplanet will be deleted from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index at the close of November 30, 2026, alongside Strategy's removal from the MSCI USA Index. This was previously flagged as a pending decision and is now finalized with an exact effective date.
updates.thesis_fit: Index removal triggers mechanical selling from benchmark-tracking funds, a known flow headwind already part of the thesis's MSCI risk factor, now confirmed with a firm date.

reports.name: Asset Entities / Strive
reports.email_summary: Strive paused Bitcoin buying and ATM sales for the first time in months as cash dipped to $462.4M.
reports.bottom_line: After weeks of steady accumulation funded by preferred-stock ATMs, Strive's treasury growth engine paused for a week with no BTC purchases or share sales, a routine but notable break in cadence worth watching for signs of financing fatigue. Share price remains highly volatile (down to $14.51 before a 16.5% gap-up), and mNAV has compressed to roughly 1.36x, modestly narrowing the arbitrage that has funded past purchases.

updates.headline: Strive pauses Bitcoin buying, skips ATM sales for a week
updates.what_happened: Strive disclosed in a Form 8-K that it purchased no bitcoin during the week ended November 20, 2026, leaving its treasury unchanged at 43,404 BTC, and sold no shares of Class A common stock, SATA, or SATS preferred through its at-the-market programs. Cash and cash equivalents declined $2.9 million to $462.4 million over the week, and the company's 505,000 shares of Strategy's STRC preferred stock lost roughly $3.2 million in fair value. Share counts were unchanged at 127,331,109 combined Class A/B shares.
updates.thesis_fit: A pause in both BTC accumulation and ATM issuance interrupts the weekly 'bitcoin-per-share' growth narrative central to the thesis, though a single quiet week does not by itself signal distress.

reports.name: BitMine Immersion

snapshot.holdings: 6,085,564 ETH (4.98% of ETH supply) plus 216 BTC, $180M Beast Industries stake, $54M Eightco (ORBS) stake, $50M other moonshots, $384M cash & marketable securities; total crypto+cash+moonshots $11.1B as of Nov 22, 2026

reports.email_summary: BitMine's weekly 8-K shows ETH holdings climbing to 6.09M tokens as total asset value slips to $11.1B on lower ETH prices.
reports.bottom_line: BitMine kept its uninterrupted weekly ETH-buying streak alive, adding 7,819 ETH even as a falling ETH price cut total disclosed treasury value to $11.1B from $11.8B the prior week. No new financing, dilution, buyback, or governance disclosures emerged in the window, leaving the thesis essentially unchanged on fundamentals while mNAV continues to trade at a discount (~0.83x) to reported NAV.
source_conflicts: BMNR share price on Nov 23 is reported inconsistently across sources: Benzinga cites a Monday close of $15.30 (+17.9%), while Robinhood shows an intraday price of $14.22 the same day — likely reflecting different intraday snapshots rather than a true data conflict.

mNAV/discount estimates differ by source and date: Cestrian Capital Research pegs BMNR at a 14% NAV discount (0.86x) as of Nov 18 close, while the BMNR mNAV Tracker shows 0.83x (17.4% discount) as of Nov 23 — consistent with a widening discount over the week but not a direct same-day conflict.

updates.headline: BitMine adds 7,819 ETH; total holdings dip to $11.1B
updates.what_happened: BitMine's weekly 8-K disclosed ETH holdings rising to 6,085,564 tokens (4.98% of total ETH supply) after buying 7,819 ETH over the prior week, extending its streak of weekly purchases since June 2025. Total crypto, cash, and moonshot holdings fell to $11.1 billion from $11.8 billion a week earlier because the ETH price used for the mark dropped to $1,713 from $1,823, even though staked ETH (5,227,037 tokens) and projected annualized staking revenue ($286M, up from a prior high of $294M) were essentially unchanged in token terms.
updates.thesis_fit: Continued disciplined weekly ETH accumulation and unchanged staking participation (~86% of ETH staked) support the accumulation leg of the thesis, but the falling ETH mark and the stock's persistent ~17% discount to NAV offset the positive on-chain progress.

updates.headline: Tom Lee frames ETH, BTC as 'hard money' on low supply growth
updates.what_happened: In commentary accompanying the weekly 8-K, Chairman Tom Lee argued ETH and BTC function as hard money, noting ETH supply had grown 1.26% since BitMine adopted its treasury strategy in June 2025, versus 0.82% for Bitcoin and much higher annualized inflation for Solana, XRP, and Cardano. He used the comparison to reinforce BitMine's ETH-centric accumulation thesis rather than announcing any new treasury-policy action.
updates.thesis_fit: This is narrative reinforcement of the existing ETH-accumulation thesis rather than a concrete new commitment on treasury policy, financing, or custody.

sector.bottom_line: Sector risk sentiment deteriorated sharply this week as MSCI's finalized index-exclusion list took effect, Bitcoin and Ether ETFs posted their worst outflows in months, Fed officials hardened toward a December hike (with Dec 9 odds near 90-95%), and widening treasury-company mNAV discounts are choking off the equity-issuance financing loop that funded years of corporate Bitcoin accumulation.

updates.headline: MSCI confirms Strategy, Metaplanet deletion; SharpLink on watch list
updates.what_happened: MSCI officially published its November index review naming Strategy for deletion from the MSCI USA Index and Metaplanet from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index, effective at the close of November 30, under its finalized 'non-operating company' screening framework. Ethereum treasury company SharpLink was not deleted outright but was placed on a new public watch list.

updates.headline: Bitcoin, Ether ETFs post largest weekly outflows in months
updates.what_happened: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $1.79 billion in net outflows for the week ending November 20, the third-largest weekly outflow on record and the fourth consecutive losing week, with BlackRock's IBIT alone shedding about $1.37 billion. Spot Ether ETFs lost an additional $305-314 million, extending an eight-week outflow streak, while Bitcoin fell from about $65,300 to below $59,000 during the week.

updates.headline: Fed December hike odds surge to 90-95% after hawkish minutes
updates.what_happened: Minutes from the October FOMC meeting, released November 18, showed almost all officials backing further tightening, with some open to a move larger than 25bp in December. CME FedWatch and prediction markets subsequently pushed December 9 hike odds to roughly 90-95%, before a broader equity selloff later cut 50bp-hike odds to zero and left a 25bp move to 4.00-4.25% as the dominant expectation.

updates.headline: SEC nominees Johnson, Levine testify at Senate Banking hearing
updates.what_happened: Steven Levine and Kristin N. Johnson appeared before the Senate Banking Committee for their SEC confirmation hearing, with discussion focused on the SEC's September 17 tokenized-stock innovation exemption. Johnson emphasized notice-and-comment rulemaking while Levine compared the exemption to early ETF exemptive orders that later led to formal rulemaking; confirming both would move the SEC from two to four commissioners.

updates.headline: CFTC nominees face Senate Agriculture hearing; chair backs CFTC spot role
updates.what_happened: The Senate Agriculture Committee held its hearing for CFTC nominees Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland on November 17, with Chairman Boozman stating the CFTC is the right regulator for the digital-asset spot market. Separately, on November 9 Coinbase, Kalshi, Payward, DRW, Jump Trading and Paradigm submitted a proposed amicus brief supporting the CFTC in ongoing market-structure litigation, and the SEC also filed its own amicus brief.

updates.headline: CFTC prediction-market rules move to White House review
updates.what_happened: The CFTC filed its 'Prediction Markets; Public Interest Determinations' rulemaking with the White House's Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs for review, advancing its claim of exclusive jurisdiction over event contracts. A coalition of 44 state attorneys general said they opposed the CFTC's prediction-market rulemaking, underscoring an ongoing state-federal jurisdiction dispute.

updates.headline: Majority of top crypto treasury firms trade below NAV, choking financing
updates.what_happened: Blockworks data cited this week showed 24 of the 25 largest crypto-treasury companies trading below the value of their holdings, with Strategy's mNAV around 1.0-1.08x (and briefly sub-1x), Metaplanet at 0.49x, and SharpLink near 0.67x as of mid-to-late November. Persistent sub-1.0x mNAV removes the equity-issuance arbitrage that funded years of corporate Bitcoin accumulation, with VanEck noting 20 companies have already retreated from Bitcoin treasury strategies in 2026 (9 full exits, 7 partial sellers).

updates.headline: CFTC approves blockchain-based derivatives exchange TLD Markets
updates.what_happened: On November 16, the CFTC designated TLD Markets, Inc. as a new derivatives exchange, confirmed in the agency's official filing record, extending the CFTC's recent run of crypto-market-infrastructure approvals.
